title: Staggered fintech adoption on loan default rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

The research question aims to determine if the adoption of algorithmic credit scoring (fintech) reduced loan default rates. Given the panel data structure where banks adopt the technology at different points in time (simplified to a single cohort adopting by period 4 in this scenario), a Difference-in-Differences (DID) methodology is appropriate. Specifically, a Two-Way Fixed Effects (TWFE) DID model will be employed.

The model is specified as:
$y_{it} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{Treated}_i + \beta_2 \cdot \text{Post}_t + \beta_3 \cdot (\text{Treated}_i \times \text{Post}_t) + \alpha_i +

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Staggered DID (Callaway-Sant'Anna or Sun-Abraham) — cohort-specific ATTs; treatment=fintech adoption
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Fintech-adopting banks reduce default rates relative to non-adopters
